woodpecker.title: Woodpecker
woodpecker.desc: The same puzzle set, in faster and faster cycles.
woodpecker.why: By reviewing the same motifs again and again, they become reflexes: you calculate less, you see more. It's like learning a language: at first you translate, then you speak.

puzzles.title: Puzzles
puzzles.desc: Tactics at your level, by theme when you want to focus.
puzzles.why: You spot a fork in 2 seconds instead of looking for it for 2 minutes. And your opponent won't be so lucky.

streak.title: Puzzle streak
streak.desc: From easiest to hardest: one mistake and you start from zero.
streak.why: The pressure rises with every puzzle. Staying clear-headed when everything hinges on one move is exactly what's missing in games.

repertoire.title: Repertoire
repertoire.desc: Your openings, reviewed move by move until they come out on their own.
repertoire.why: No more playing the first ten moves by feel: you reach the middlegame on familiar ground, with time on the clock.

evaluation.title: Position evaluation
evaluation.desc: Who is better, and by how much? Judge at a glance.
evaluation.why: Knowing where you stand before calculating means picking the right variations instead of trying them all.

analyse.title: Game analysis
analyse.desc: Go back over your games, especially the losses.
analyse.why: Your mistakes become your program, instead of repeating game after game.

coach.title: Tailored session
coach.desc: I read your last 200 Lichess games, spot the endgames that cost you points and build your session.
coach.why: You work on what makes you lose, not on what you already know. Training time is scarce: might as well aim right.

finales.title: Endgames
finales.desc: Rooks, pawns, minor pieces: the essential endgames.
finales.why: An extra pawn is worth nothing if you don't know how to promote it.

aveugle.title: Blindfold play
aveugle.desc: The position appears, disappears, then you play from memory on an empty board.
aveugle.why: Your visualization gets trained: you calculate further, even with the pieces in front of you.

coordonnees.title: Coordinates
coordonnees.desc: Find e4 without thinking, on a board with no letters or numbers.
coordonnees.why: A square you name quickly is a variation you calculate without getting lost along the way.

title: Albert
Stein
albert.line: I'm the tactics Bishop: I see the diagonals before you see the trap. And I see them diagonally, of course.

title: Aaron,
the King
aaron.line: I take the initiative from the first move and never give it back. Even at dinner, ask Lizy.

title: Lizy,
the Queen
lizy.line: Your small advantage, I turn it into a full point. Without trembling, and without asking Aaron's opinion.

title: Ray,
the mystery
ray.kicker: ALBERT · A PROF IN THE SHADOWS
ray.line: Ray plays with his eyes closed. He'll introduce himself… as soon as he finds the door.

beginner.name: Beginner
beginner.hint: I sometimes mix up the bishop and the rook.
beginner.line: Perfect: no bad habits to get rid of. Well, almost.

amateur.name: Amateur
amateur.hint: I know the Scholar's mate. From both sides.
amateur.line: The ideal level: strong enough to blunder in style, curious enough to stop.

confirmed.name: Advanced
confirmed.hint: My Najdorf holds up without a cheat sheet.
confirmed.line: Nice. We'll polish what's stuck, without pulling the Scholar's mate on you again.

expert.name: Expert
expert.line: Ah. I'll have to review my notes, then.

pro.name: Pro
pro.hint: People call me “Master”, and they're not being ironic.
pro.line: A pro here? The puzzles are going to sweat. So am I.

rating.label: Gain Elo
rating.line: Elo, noted. We'll start by no longer giving it away.

blunders.label: Stop giving away my queen
blunders.line: A queen given away is a gift nobody asked for. We'll learn to keep her.

fun.label: Have fun
fun.line: Excellent choice. Nobody ever improved while bored.

understanding.label: Understand what I play
understanding.line: The finest ambition: one move you understand is worth ten moves you recite.

kasparov.label: Snatch a draw from Kasparov
kasparov.line: A draw against Garry? That'll take Woodpecker. Lots of Woodpecker.

map.title: My game path
map.desc: Visualisation, calculation, endgames: move from square to square and face the bosses.

coach.title: Automatic or custom training session
coach.desc: Lizy builds your session from your Lichess games, or you pick the modules and durations yourself.

repertoire.title: Automatic or custom repertoire
repertoire.desc: Aaron builds it with the openings you play on Lichess, or you put it together move by move.

modules.title: Training modules, open access
modules.desc: Puzzles, Woodpecker, endgames, coordinates… Open whichever you like, whenever you want.
